title: Can we build all three of these triangles?
description: The video draws three triangles from a side, the angle between, and a second side: three, seventy five, seven; six, twenty five, three; and three, one hundred and twenty, eight. Each is drawn the same way as the example in the book, and each is checked with the protractor and the ruler.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same four moves build every triangle, whatever the angle. Watch for children who think a very small or a wide angle cannot make a triangle.

source: Construct triangles for the following measurements where the angle is included between the sides: (a) 3 cm, 75°, 7 cm (b) 6 cm, 25°, 3 cm (c) 3 cm, 120°, 8 cm
video_script.why: The child can draw one triangle from two sides and the angle between them and now draws three, with a small angle and a wide angle.
video_script.substitution: Draw the first side as the base, make the angle at one end, mark the second side along the new arm and join.
video_script.anchor: three sets of a side, the angle between, and a side: three, seventy five, seven; six, twenty five, three; three, one hundred and twenty, eight
video_script.payoff_line: All three triangles can be built

final_answer.spoken: all three triangles can be built

maths_rules: (a) 3 cm, 75°, 7 cm: third side squared = 9 + 49 - 42 x cos 75° = 47.1 so the third side = 6.87 cm, about 6.9 cm
(b) 6 cm, 25°, 3 cm: third side squared = 36 + 9 - 36 x cos 25° = 12.4 so the third side = 3.52 cm, about 3.5 cm
(c) 3 cm, 120°, 8 cm: third side squared = 9 + 64 + 24 = 97 so the third side = 9.85 cm, about 9.8 cm
each angle is between 0° and 180°, so the free ends can always be joined
video_script.design: Three sets of measurements are shown once in the anchor band. The same four moves are drawn for each set in turn, and the check is done at the end.

<bookmark mark='third'/>The third is three centimetres, one hundred and twenty degrees and eight centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we build all three triangles?
